name: Men-an-tol

attributes.attribute: a healing stone of Cornwall, near Lanyon
the sick were pulled through its hole and rolled on the grass
brass pins on the rock gave an answer to a question

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Men-an-tol is a Cornish place of healing. Near the village of Lanyon stands a great stone with a hole in its center. The stone was famous for curing the sickness of children and the pain of the spine. In the old rite, the sick were pulled through the hole and then rolled on the grass three times, or three times three. The stone could also be used for the future. If a person laid two brass pins on the rock and asked a question, the moving pins gave the answer.

okr.objective: Document Men-an-tol, the Cornish healing stone near Lanyon.
